description: Cluster from the fz-f98.9 graduation measurement. reduce/3 param0, reverse/1 param0, to_list/1 param0 declare protocol::Enumerable.t but receive any (~104 site-hits across the matrix). The protocol's generic t(a) boundary erases the concrete element/collection type to any when a value crosses it -- the protocol analog of fz-f98.8 (which recovered struct field types at destructure). This is the dominant ROOT: the any it produces then floods arithmetic operators downstream (see sibling cluster). Fix: preserve / recover the concrete element type across the t(a) protocol boundary so Enumerable consumers don't graduate to any. Overlaps f98.5/f98.6 over-monomorphization (the any axis).
title: Enumerable protocol boundary erases element type to any (t(a) -> any)
